verses.text: I told myself, “Come on, let's see what having fun gets you. Go ahead and enjoy it.” That too turned out to be vapor.
I said of laughter, “That's foolishness,” and of having fun, “What does it actually accomplish?”

I thought hard about how to cheer myself with wine while letting wisdom guide me, and how to get hold of foolishness. I wanted to see what was worth doing under heaven in all the days people have to live.
I took on huge projects. I built houses for myself and planted my own vineyards.
I made gardens and parks and planted all kinds of fruit trees in them.
I built pools to water the grove where the trees grew.
I bought men and women as servants, and others were born in my household. I owned more herds and flocks than anyone in Jerusalem before me.
I collected silver and gold and the treasures of kings and provinces. I got men and women to sing for me, and all kinds of musical instruments that people love.
I became greater and gained more than anyone in Jerusalem before me. My wisdom stayed with me too.
Whatever caught my eye, I let myself have it. I held back no joy from my heart. I took pleasure in everything I'd worked for, and that was my share of all that work.
Then I looked at everything my hands had made and all the effort I'd put into it. It was all vapor, like chasing the wind. There was no gain under the sun.
I turned to look at wisdom, madness, and foolishness. What can the next king do? Only what was already done long ago.
I saw that wisdom beats foolishness as surely as light beats darkness.
Wise people can see where they're going, while fools walk in the dark. Still, I saw that the same fate catches up with them both.
I thought, “What happens to a fool will happen to me too. So what did all my wisdom get me?” I told myself that this too was vapor.
No one remembers the wise forever, any more than they remember fools. In the days ahead both will be long forgotten. Wise people have to die just like fools.
So I hated life. Everything people do under the sun weighed on me. It's all vapor, like chasing the wind.
I hated all the work I'd done under the sun, because I have to leave it to whoever comes after me.
Who knows whether they'll be wise or foolish? Either way, they'll control everything I worked for and used my wisdom to build under the sun. This too is vapor.
So I started to lose heart over all the work I'd done under the sun.
Someone can work with wisdom, knowledge, and skill, then have to leave everything to someone who didn't lift a finger for it. This too is vapor and a great wrong.
What do people get from all the work and all the stress they put themselves through under the sun?
Their days are full of sorrow, and their work brings grief. Even at night their heart gets no rest. This too is vapor.
There's nothing better than to eat, drink, and enjoy something good in your work. I saw that this too comes from God's hand.
Who could eat or enjoy life more than I could?

God gives wisdom, knowledge, and joy to the person who pleases him. He gives sinners the work of gathering and piling things up to hand over to someone who pleases him. This too is vapor, like chasing the wind.
